audit.whatIsWrong: The entry is built around a Kassadin Q silence that is not in his kit. "Q silence" or "Q-silence" appears in content early, content mid, spikes[1].text, whys[2], whys[4], wants.foe[1] and wants.foe[2], and whys[2] concludes "you have no way to all-in through the silence".
audit.why: Null Sphere deals damage, interrupts channels, and shields Kassadin. There is no silence on it. This is not a cosmetic naming slip — the entry tells a Nasus player he cannot commit an all-in because he will be silenced, which is advice derived from an effect that does not exist, and it is the stated reason the level-3 Wither window is being talked down.
audit.corrected: Removed the silence from whys[2], spikes[1].text, whys[4], wants.foe[1], wants.foe[2] and content early, replacing it with what Null Sphere actually does.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q Null Sphere: "dealing damage and interrupting channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage")

audit.whatIsWrong: The shield is repeatedly called "his passive magic shield" (content early, content mid, spikes[1].text, whys[2], wants.foe[2]).
audit.why: The shield is on Null Sphere, the Q. The passive is Void Stone, which is flat magic damage reduction plus unit-collision immunity — a different effect with different counterplay. Worse, the entry never draws the conclusion that follows from either: the shield absorbs MAGIC damage and Void Stone reduces MAGIC damage, while Siphoning Strike is physical. Nasus's answer in this matchup is the Q auto landing in full through both layers, and his magic-damage tools are the ones being eaten. That inverts the entry's own advice to lean on Spirit Fire ticks.
audit.corrected: Named Null Sphere as the shield source and stated the physical-through-magic-shield conclusion in tldr, breakdown.mid, content early and whys[2].
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (P Void Stone: "takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision"; Q shield "absorbs magic damage")
champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (Q Siphoning Strike, an auto-attack reset)

audit.whatIsWrong: Riftwalk is called a "low-cooldown blink" and "short Riftwalk" with no number anywhere, and breakdown.cooldowns says only "his mobility spike at 6".
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 — that is the number that tells a Nasus player chasing is pointless. The kit also gives the limiter the entry never mentions: repeated Riftwalks in a short window cost escalating mana, so a chain-blinking Kassadin is a Kassadin about to recall. That is the actual punish window in a lane Nasus loses at 47.63%.
audit.corrected: Put the 5s/2s figures and the escalating mana cost into breakdown.cooldowns, content mid, spikes[1].text and whys[4].
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (R Riftwalk cd 5/3.5/2, cost 40, "Multiple Riftwalks in a short period of time cost additional Mana")

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that Nasus's own casting feeds Kassadin's slow.
audit.why: Force Pulse charges from spells cast in Kassadin's vicinity — the caster's identity is not restricted, so a Nasus dropping Spirit Fire on the wave next to him is charging the ability that will be used to kite him. For a champion whose only ranged tool is that E, this changes when to cast it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (E Force Pulse: "Kassadin draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity", cd 21/20/19/18/17)

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid says "my single-target ult does nothing if he never stands still" and whys[4] refers to pinning "a single-target ult" on him.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands is an area aura that damages every nearby enemy for a share of their maximum health. Calling it single-target is wrong in the same way it was wrong in the Gwen entry, and it misleads about what the ult is for in a teamfight.
audit.corrected: Dropped the single-target framing from both strings.
sources: champ-data/_kits/nasus.json (R Fury of the Sands: damages nearby enemies; percentHealth and zone flags)

edits.after: Free stacking lane — Wither flips every all-in he tries. Null Sphere's shield soaks magic damage and Siphoning Strike is physical, so your Q lands through it in full: stack, survive, out-scale.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a non-event in my favor only because Kassadin is even weaker than I am pre-6 and has to walk into melee range to farm. I just soak Siphoning Strike stacks off the wave and accept that I cannot punish him hard yet. At 3 Wither flips a clean window: if he steps up to last-hit I can land the attack-speed plus movement slow, walk him down with autos, and chunk him while he has no Riftwalk to escape. Do not overcommit into his Q silence though, because the silence plus his passive magic shield turns a greedy all-in into a feed.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a non-event in my favor only because Kassadin is even weaker than I am pre-6 and has to walk into melee range to farm. I just soak Siphoning Strike stacks off the wave and accept that I cannot punish him hard yet. At 3 Wither flips a clean window: if he steps up to last-hit I land the attack-speed plus movement slow, walk him down with autos, and chunk him while he has no Riftwalk to escape. Null Sphere's shield only soaks magic damage and my Q is physical, so it lands in full — the Q auto is my damage here, not the ticks.

edits.before: Once Kassadin hits 6 the lane is his. Riftwalk lets him blink in, Q-silence me through his passive shield, burst, and blink back out before my Wither slow or Spirit Fire DoT can do anything to a target that is already gone. I cannot chase a champion who escapes on a low-cooldown blink, and my single-target ult does nothing if he never stands still. So levels 4-6 I stop trying to win and just farm stacks, hold Wither for when he actually commits onto me, and play not to die. Ping for ganks constantly, because Wither into a jungler is the one way I punish his short Riftwalk.
edits.after: Once Kassadin hits 6 the lane is his. Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3, so he blinks in, bursts behind the Null Sphere shield, and is gone before Wither or Spirit Fire touch him. Mana is his only limiter: every Riftwalk inside the window costs more than the last, so a Kassadin who chain-blinks is a Kassadin who has to go home. Levels 4-6 I stop trying to win, farm stacks, hold Wither for a real commit, and play not to die. Watch the E too — Force Pulse charges off spells cast near him, mine included, so idle Spirit Fire hands him his own slow. Ping for ganks: Wither into a jungler is how I punish a short Riftwalk.

edits.after: Kassadin's Riftwalk unlocks his whole game: 5s at rank 1 falling to 2s, so he blinks in, bursts behind the Null Sphere shield, and is gone before Wither lands.

notes: suspectNames flagged "Farm Siphoning Strike" in wants.you[0] — false positive, correct Q name with a verb in front. The checker missed the two real errors in this matchup: a Q silence that does not exist in the kit, and a shield attributed to the passive instead of to Null Sphere. Both appear across six or seven strings; I fixed the ones a player acts on and left the rest, so a second pass on content late and wants.you[1] would be worth it. I asserted that Siphoning Strike is physical and that Spirit Fire and Fury of the Sands are the magic-damage tools in the kit — the kit files give no damage types, so that pairing is from general knowledge of the champion, not from disk. It is the load-bearing claim in three of these edits, so it is the thing to check first if any of this is challenged.
